thesis: The speaker argues that allocator decision-making has historically relied too heavily on a manager's recent stock price performance rather than conducting a fundamental analysis of the manager's attributes, such as their income statement, balance sheet, and cash flow. This imbalance exists because the industry lacks an equivalent to the deep financial work typically applied when evaluating individual stocks.
